reading: Two single cells sit on opposite long edges. Each becomes a full line across the short dimension, and the pair of lines repeats with the same spacing and alternating colours to the far end of the grid.

slots.orientation: lines run across the short side of the grid (perpendicular to the long axis)
slots.period: the offset between the two seeds along the long axis
slots.colours: alternate seed1, seed2, seed1, ... starting at the first seed and continuing to the grid end

why: every output line lies at seed position + k*period along the long axis, coloured by k's parity

reading: Each red (2) cell gets yellow (4) on its four diagonal neighbours; each blue (1) cell gets orange (7) on its four orthogonal neighbours. Other colours are left alone.

new_rows.name: diag_of_red
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diagoff(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !orth(DY, DX).
diag_of_red(Y, X) :- cell(Y0, X0, C), C = 2, diagoff(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, B).

new_rows.name: orth_of_blue
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
orth_of_blue(Y, X) :- cell(Y0, X0, C), C = 1, orth(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, B).

why: the 4s are exactly the diagonal neighbours of 2s, the 7s exactly the orthogonal neighbours of 1s
invariants: cells of colours 6 and 8 get nothing

reading: A fixed colour substitution applied to every cell: 1<->5, 2<->6, 3<->4, 8<->9.
why: each input colour maps to the same output colour in every pair

reading: Pairs of blue (1) cells on opposite borders are joined by a blue line; every red (2) rectangle the line passes through turns entirely blue.

new_rows.name: hit
new_rows.datalog:
one(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 1.
line(Y, X) :- one(Y, X1), one(Y, X2), px(Y, X, C), X1 < X, X < X2.
line(Y, X) :- one(Y1, X), one(Y2, X), px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.
crossed(O) :- line(Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), C = 2, obj(O, Y, X).
hit(Y, X) :- line(Y, X).
hit(Y, X) :- crossed(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: the changed cells are exactly the line cells between two 1s on a row or column plus all cells of 2-objects the line meets; key 0->1, 2->1

reading: Each single coloured cell becomes a full horizontal line of its colour; the grid is cut into horizontal bands at the midpoints between seeds, and each band gets left and right border columns in its seed's colour (top and bottom grid rows are also drawn in the colour of the first and last band).

slots.seeds: the isolated coloured cells, ordered by row
slots.bands: row ranges split halfway between consecutive seeds
slots.drawn: full row at each seed, columns 0 and W-1 over its band, row 0 in first seed colour, row H-1 in last seed colour

why: every non-background output cell is a seed row, a band side column, or the top/bottom row, coloured by its band's seed
invariants: interior cells off the seed rows stay background

reading: A small multicoloured key pattern is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, scaled up by the block size, and used to colour the large grey (8) silhouette, which has the same shape as the rotated key.
verb: rotate and scale key onto silhouette

frame.verb: rotate and scale key onto silhouette

slots.silhouette: the large single-colour (8) object made of k x k blocks
slots.transform: rotate key 90 degrees clockwise, upscale by k
slots.paint: each silhouette block takes the colour of the matching rotated key cell

why: the silhouette's block mask equals the rotated key's non-background mask, and each block's output colour equals the rotated key cell

reading: The input is tiled 2x2; then every background cell diagonally adjacent to a coloured cell becomes azure (8).

new_rows.name: diag_bg
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diagoff(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !orth(DY, DX).
diag_bg(Y, X) :- cell(Y0, X0, C), diagoff(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, B), B = 0.

why: output = 2x2 tiling of input, plus 8 on exactly the background cells diagonal to a non-background cell (no wrap, coloured cells never overwritten)

reading: Three coloured cells mark three corners of a square box. A grey (5) cell is placed at the box centre, and a copy of each corner cell is placed one diagonal step from the centre toward that corner.

slots.centre: centre of their bounding box, filled with 5
slots.copies: for each corner, its colour at centre + sign(corner - centre) (one diagonal step)

why: the added cells are exactly the centre (5) and the three one-step diagonal copies of the corner colours

reading: Every single-colour 4-connected group of one or two cells turns green (3); groups of three or more cells stay.

new_rows.name: small4
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
nz(Y, X, C) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0.
same(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- nz(Y, X, C), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, nz(Y2, X2, C).
deg(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- same(Y, X, Y2, X2).
big(Y, X) :- deg(Y, X, N), N > 1.
big(Y, X) :- same(Y, X, Y2, X2), deg(Y2, X2, N), N > 1.
small4(Y, X) :- nz(Y, X, C), !big(Y, X).

why: a non-zero cell becomes 3 iff its 4-connected same-colour component has fewer than 3 cells (8-connectivity is wrong: pair 2 cell (6,5))

reading: A full grey (5) wall runs along one edge. Every other bar sweeps toward the wall, painting its colour into each background cell until it hits the wall or another bar.

new_rows.name: bars
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rc(Y, C, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
cc(X, C, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
wallrow(Y) :- rc(Y, C, N), w(M), N = M + 1.
wallcol(X) :- cc(X, C, N), h(M), N = M + 1.
wall(Y, X) :- wallrow(Y), cell(Y, X, C).
wall(Y, X) :- wallcol(X), cell(Y, X, C).
bars(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !wall(Y, X).

why: from each bar cell a ray of its colour runs perpendicular to the bar toward the wall and stops at the first non-background cell
invariants: cells on the far side of each bar from the wall
